glosses: Having an absolute or (more often) relative lack of light.

examples.text: The room was too dark for reading.

They burned the old gun that used to stand in the dark corner up in the garret, close to the stuffed fox that always grinned so fiercely. Perhaps the reason why he seemed in such a ghastly rage was that he did not come by his death fairly. And why else was he put away up there out of sight?—and so magnificent a brush as he had too.

[Rural solar plant] schemes are of little help to industry or other heavy users of electricity. Nor is solar power yet as cheap as the grid. For all that, the rapid arrival of electric light to Indian villages is long overdue. When the national grid suffers its next huge outage, as it did in July 2012 when hundreds of millions were left in the dark, look for specks of light in the villages.

glosses: Conducive to hopelessness; depressing or bleak.

examples.text: The Great Depression was a dark time.

glosses: Lacking progress in science or the arts.

examples.text: The dark ages began after the collapse of the Roman Empire.

 Could not want light who taught the world to see.

glosses: Extremely sad, depressing, or somber, typically due to, or marked by, a tragic or undesirable event.

examples.text: September 11, 2001, the day when four terrorist attacks destroyed the Twin Towers and the Pentagon, is often referred to as America’s dark day.

examples.text: The ending of this book is rather dark.

glosses: Qui est peu éclairé ; qui reçoit peu de lumière ; qui est obscur.

examples.text: Aucune lumière n’était demeurée ni dans les chambres basses ni dans les corridors ; de temps en temps seulement un éclair livide illuminait les appartements sombres d’un reflet bleuâtre qui disparaissait aussitôt.

glosses: Qui est moins éclatant, qui est plus foncé que les autres, en parlant d’une teinte, d’une couleur.

examples.text: […] puis il […] se coiffa d’un toquet de velours noir sans plume ni pierreries, s’enveloppa d’un manteau de couleur sombre […]

glosses: Qui est mélancolique, morne, taciturne ou chagrin.

examples.text: Son appartement, comme son costume, était celui d’une veuve. Tout y était d’un caractère sombre : étoffes, murailles, meubles.

[…] et debout près de la barre, Jean Donnard, grave et sombre, se signa, comme il avait coutume de faire chaque fois qu’il partait vers le large.

glosses: Qui est inquiétant ou menaçant.

examples.text: Émile doit rejoindre, dès dix heures du matin, au deuxième jour de la mobilisation. Il est désolé. Les plus sombres pressentiments le poignent.
